paper.title: Non-stochastic Best Arm Identification and Hyperparameter Optimization

unmapped: Loss of arm i on its k-th pull is a deterministic real number l_{i,k} fixed by an oblivious adversary; each arm's loss sequence converges to a limit nu_i, with unknown convergence rate (envelope gamma_i(t))
Goal is to identify argmin_i nu_i (limit values), not the arm with best mean; guarantees are deterministic in terms of the max envelope inverse gamma_bar^{-1}
Budget B (total number of pulls) given to the algorithm
settings.definition_quote: Non-stochastic (proposed in this work) : For all $i \in [n]$, $k \geq 1$, let $\ell_{i,k} \in \R$ be generated by an oblivious adversary and assume $\nu_i = \displaystyle\lim_{\tau \rightarrow \infty} \ell_{i,\tau}$ exists. The goal is to identify $\arg\min_i \nu_i$ while minimizing $\sum_{i=1}^n T_i$.

symbols.z_max: max_{i=2..n} i*(1 + gamma_bar^{-1}((nu_i - nu_1)/2)), with arms sorted by limit value
symbols.gamma_bar: max_i gamma_i(t), the max over arms of the smallest non-increasing envelope |l_{i,t} - nu_i| <= gamma_i(t)

conditions: each arm's loss sequence has a limit nu_i

source.label: adaptive

results.notes: Sufficient budget (deterministic): if B > z, Successive Halving returns the best arm. Recorded as a sample-complexity bound; n is K.

symbols.gbar_inv_i: gamma_bar^{-1}((nu_i - nu_1)/2) = min{t : max_j gamma_j(t) <= (nu_i - nu_1)/2}

conditions: each arm's loss sequence has a limit nu_i

source.label: adaptive
source.quote: z \leq 2 \lceil \log_2(n) \rceil ( n + \sum_{i=2,\dots,n} \bar{\gamma}^{-1} ( \tfrac{ \nu_i -\nu_1 }{2} ) ). If the budget $B>z$ then the best arm is returned from the algorithm.

results.notes: Looser, sum form of the same theorem.

conditions: each arm's loss sequence has a limit nu_i
B is a multiple of n

source.label: thm:prettygood
source.quote: For a budget $B$ and set of $n$ arms, define $\widehat{i}_{SH}$ as the output of the Successive Halving algorithm. Then \nu_{\widehat{i}_{SH}} - \nu_1 \leq \lceil\log_2(n)\rceil 2 \bar{\gamma}( \lfloor \tfrac{ B }{n \lceil \log_2(n) \rceil } \rfloor ).

results.notes: Budget B written as T (total number of pulls). Simple regret measured on limit values nu.
